description: 2nd-year Data Science student at IISER Bhopal looking to build something creative with AI/ML, data & space — looking for curious builders in coding, space science, data viz, design & storytelling who are ready to turn ideas into something awesome!
summary: Pyro-Harmony, is an interactive geospatial analytics prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to address the official challenge of harmonizing active-fire observations from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments. For over two decades, NASA has tracked global wildfires using MODIS, which features an approximate one kilometre spatial resolution and has operated since 2000 alongside the sharper VIIRS instrument, which uses ~375-meter pixels and has been active since 2012. Because these varying pixel sizes cause the exact same fire activity to be recorded differently, raw daily detection counts exhibit an artificial surge following the introduction of VIIRS, rendering multi-decade trend analysis and seasonal anomaly detection difficult without explicit correction.
details:
Methodology

• Unified Confidence Filtering: Standardises sensor confidence scales by mapping VIIRS categorical flags (low/nominal/high) to 20/60/90 alongside MODIS's 0–100 scale, dropping detections below 30 across both instruments to maintain a consistent detection floor.

• Instrument-Level Grouping: Aggregates observations by sensor family rather than individual satellite platforms (combining Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 under VIIRS).

• Empirical Overlap Rescaling: Rescales per sensor daily counts to the best covered sensor using a measured conversion ratio derived from collocated overlap days where both instruments observed active fire (requiring a minimum of 5 overlap days; defaulting to a factor of 1.0 otherwise). On a synthetic 2002–2024 benchmark with a known gentle trend, this method reduced an artificial +304% post-2012 jump down to +11.7% (calibration 𝑅2 = 0.867, RMSE = 2.91 MW across 9,767 matchups).

• Footprint & Intensity Normalisation: Divides each detection's scan-by-track footprint by its sensor's nadir cell area to compute the Effective Sensor Footprint (ESFP), and multiplies Fire Radiative Power (FRP) by ESFP to derive the Harmonised Fire Intensity Index (HFII).

Fire Intelligence & Analytics

• Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN): Groups hotspots into distinct fire events using density-based clustering (550 m radius, 3 minimum points, 12-hour window, adapted from operational GISTDA parameters) without requiring a preset cluster count, filtering out isolated noise and returning convex hulls for the largest events.

• Regional Stratification (K-Means): Partitions spatial activity into 𝑘 = 4 regional intensity regimes ranked by total FRP.

• Climatology & Anomaly Detection: Computes rolling 15-day percentiles (10th, 50th, 90th, 95th) by day of year to establish seasonal onset and cessation baselines. Daily counts are z-scored against a ±7-day window across other years, while monthly totals are evaluated using leave-one-year-out standard deviations so extreme seasons do not distort their own reference band.

• Forecasting: Pairs a seasonal climatology baseline with a global LightGBM (Tweedie) gradientboosting model trained on a 2∘ × day grid using leave-one-fire-season-out cross-validation. At runtime, LightGBM predictions are served only on forecast horizons where back testing outperformed the seasonal prior (such as the 14-day horizon on the pooled archive, MASE 1.945 vs 1.983); otherwise, the system falls back transparently to the seasonal baseline.

• Incident Commander Briefing: Translates statistical anomalies into a decision-support summary featuring a heuristic threat score (Threat = max𝑧 + 0.5 × streak days + min(2,recent mean ÷ 25), triggering Watch at 3.5 and Critical at 6.0), 30-day trend comparisons, and active cluster summaries.

Architecture & Technology Stack

• Backend & Data Processing: Built in Python with FastAPI, Pandas, and NumPy for high-throughput ingestion and harmonisation, supported by server-side memoisation (~11 ms warm briefing queries) and a bounded stratified archive reader.

• Machine Learning & Statistics: Uses Scikit-learn, SciPy, and LightGBM for clustering, percentile climatology, z-score anomaly detection, and horizon-gated forecasting.

• Frontend & Geospatial Visualisation: Built with React, Vite, and MapLibre GL, featuring an interactive 3D globe that transitions smoothly into a 2D map, adaptive frame-rate scaling for lowpower hardware, and custom, zero-dependency SVG charts for the Burning Activity Calendar and climatology envelopes (~55 KB zipped initial payload).

• Reliability & Scope: Verified with 149 automated tests (smoke, security, and archive integrity). Pyro-Harmony is explicitly framed as a research and planning prototype rather than an operational emergency-alert system.

Space Agency Data Usage

• Historical & Multi-Year Archive Data: Integrates bulk active-fire exports from NASA MODIS Collection 6.1 (Aqua and Terra satellites, ~1 km resolution) and NASA/NOAA VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 satellites, ~375 m resolution). In our reference environment, the ingestion pipeline processes 15 FIRMS archive exports (~10.3 GB, 126.2 million total rows) into a merged analytical console dataset of 1,799,078 detections spanning 2023-09-30 to 2026-07-05 (131,226 MODIS and 1,667,852 VIIRS records).

• Near-Real-Time Open Feeds & Area API: Connects directly to NASA FIRMS's four open 24-hour global active-fire feeds (MODIS plus Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 VIIRS) for on-the-fly harmonisation and clustering without requiring user credentials, alongside the FIRMS Area API for 1–5 day regional queries.

• Metadata & Sensor Parameters: Uses official FIRMS observation attributes—including latitude, longitude, acquisition date/time, scan/track pixel dimensions, confidence flags, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP)—to compute nadir-normalised footprints and cross-sensor intensity indices.
